          CROSS-REBUTTAL TESTIMONY AND EXHIBITS OF CHRISTINE M. MAGERS, CWB


 1                                   I.       INTRODUCTION

 2   Q:      WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR CROSS-REBUTTAL TESTIMONY?

 3   A:      The purpose of my cross-rebuttal testimony is to respond to the Direct Testimony of Rae

 4           Lynn Schneider Reinecke filed on Behalf ofthe Segment K13/K51 Landowners, Cherokee

 5           Creek Partners, and Bonnie Helene McAnelly, Individually and as Trustee of the 2025

 6           Homestead Trust and the Bonnie Helene McAnelly 2023 Trust (Interchange Item No.

 7           4204).


 8   Q:      ARE YOU THE SAME CHRISTINE MAGERS THAT CAUSED TO BE FILED

 9           TESTIMONY ON MAY 13, 2026 ON BEHALF OF C.E. STEPHENS PROPERTIES,

10           LLC.

11   A:      Yes.



     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                   1          Cross-Rebuttal Testimony & Exhibits
     PUC Docket No. 59475                                            of Christine M. Magers, CWB
  1   Q:    WHAT ROUTE DOES MS. REINECKE PROPOSE?

 2   A:    Ms. Reinecke proposes a new routing sequence referred to as Cherokee Creek G (Route

 3         CCG). She proposes this route as an alternative to Route 894. Route 894 is identified by

 4         the Applicants as the route that best meets the requirements of Texas Utilities Code 37.056

 5         (c)(4(AHD) and Commission Substantive Rule 25.10(b)(3)(B). Route 894 is comprised of

 6         the following links: AO-Al-A2-Bl-B21-C4-D12-C5-E52-Fl-F31-F32-F20-F23-G72-

 7         G73-G82-G13-G51-G52-Ill-H41-H42-J21-J22-J23-J27-J4-Kll-K7-J16-K13-K51-K52-

 8         Mll-M12-N3-1?2-Rl-Tl-T2-Z2.


 9   Q:    WHAT LINKS COMPRISE ROUTE CCG?

10   A:    Route CCG consists ofthe following link sequence: AO-Al-A2-Bl-B21-C4-D12-C5-E52-

11         Fl-F31-F32-F20-F23-G72-G73-G82-G13-G2-G6-Il-J31-J32-J33-J6-K62-K42-M31-L4-

12         M22-M23-M5-N4-03-1?2-Rl-Tl-T2-Z2.


13   Q:    HOW DOES ROUTE CCG DIFFER FROM ROUTE 894?

14   A:    These two routes share several of the same links in the same order starting from the east,

15         at the Bell County East Switch, towards the west as follows: AO-Al-A2-Bl-B21-C4-D12-

16         C5-E52-Fl-F31-F32-F20-F23-G72-G73-G82-G13. At the western end of Link G13, near

17         Briggs, Texas, the two routes utilize different links until link P-2 northwest of Menard,

18         Texas. The routes then utilize the same links, P2-R1-Tl-T2-Z2, to the western end of the

19         project at the Big Hill Substation.


20         From the western end of Link G13, Route 894 utilizes a northern running link sequence as

21         follows:   G51-G52-Ill -H41-H42-J21-J22-J23 -J27-J4-K 11-K7-J16-K13 -K51-K52-M11-

22         M12-N3. Whereas Route CCG utilizes a southern running link sequence from the western




     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                   2           Cross-Rebuttal Testimony & Exhibits
     PUC Docket No. 59475                                             of Christine M. Magers, CWB
  1         end ofLink G13 as follows: G2-G6-Il-J31-J32-J33-J6-K62-K42-M31-L4-M22-M23-M5-

 2         N4-03.


 3   Q:    IN YOUR DIRECT TESTIMONY YOU ADDRESSED CONCERNS WITH

 4         FRAGMENTATION             OF    A    LANDOWNER'S          PROPERTY.         DOES     MS.

 5         REINECKE'S CCG ROUTE RESULT IN FRAGMENTATION OF PROPERTY?

 6   A:    Yes. For example, Link N4 splits Sola Fe Ranch owned by the Stephens family identified

 7         as Property ID 480, 481, and 482. It also splits a ranch, owned by the Gainer Family,

 8         identified as Property ID 451, 452, 453, 454, 455,456, 457, and 458. Based on the Menard

 9         County Appraisal District parcel owner name and mailing address information, this ranch

10         extends beyond the property' s identified in the Applicant' s EA.


11         A portion of N4 is identified as parallel to property across when it's actually across the

12         middle of both the Stephens' Sola Fe Ranch and the Gainer ranch. These two properties

13         were quickly found using publicly available data; therefore, for there is a likelihood of

14         there being more similar ranches that are not properly identified as continuous single

15         properties. Accordingly, routes using Link N4, including Route CCG, would result in

16         fragmentation.


17   Q:    DID ANY INTERVENORS DISCUSS LINK N4 OR INCLUDE LINK N4 IN THEIR

18         RECOMMENDED ROUTES?

19   A:    Yes. Ms. Reinecke's proposed new alternative Route CCG includes Link N4.


20   Q:    PLEASE DESCRIBE PROBLEMS WITH ROUTES THAT INCLUDE LINK N4.

21   A:    Based upon my review of the information provided in the EA regarding Link N4, some of

22         the information, such as portions of Links that parallel property and parallel compatible

23         corridors, appear to be incorrect.

     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                   3           Cross-Rebuttal Testimony & Exhibits
     PUC Docket No. 59475                                             of Christine M. Magers, CWB
  1   Q:    PLEASE EXPLAIN THE EA INFORMATION PROBLEM REGARDING LINK N4.

 2   A:    The problem relates to the length the Applicants claim is parallel to "apparent" property

 3         boundaries for routes that include Link N4. The database the Applicants use for identifying

 4         "apparent" property boundaries are electronic county tax appraisal maps of their property

 5         tax parcels. Because they did not even group parcels by property owner, this incorrectly

 6         assumes that property ownership boundaries and property tax parcel boundaries are

 7         identical. It is common for a landowner' s property to include multiple contiguous property

 8         tax parcels as described above. In that situation, the Applicants could route a line along

 9         property tax parcel boundaries and claim it is parallel to "apparent" property boundaries

10         even though it is not on the property' s actual boundary. To illustrate this problem, see

11         Exhibit CMM-1 with both the county parcels and the actual property boundaries for the

12         Stephens Ranch on Link N4.


13         As shown in the EA, Link N4 is shown as parallel with the boundary between Property ID

14         480 on the north side ofthe link and Property's ID as 481 and 482 on the south side of the

15         link. Based on review of the spatial data provided in response to Hodge/Schwertner

16         Question No. 1-11, the Applicants have included the length of this portion of Link N4 in

17         its statistics for "length of route parallel to apparent property boundaries" and "total length

18         of route parallel to existing compatible rights-of-way". However, based on property

19         records, Property IDs 480, 481, and 482 are shown as four property tax parcels, but are

20         owned by the same landowner. The effect of doing so makes Link N4, and any route that

21         includes Link N4, look more favorable than it is.




     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                    4            Cross-Rebuttal Testimony & Exhibits
     PUC Docket No. 59475                                               of Christine M. Magers, CWB
  1   Q:    WHAT IS YOUR RECOMMENDATION REGARDING LINK N4?

 2   A:    Based on the testimony of other intervenor witnesses and the issues discussed above, I do

 3         not believe the Commission should approve a route that includes Link N4.


 4   Q:    ISTHEREABETTERALTERNATIVE TOUSINGROUTE CCG?

 5   A:    Yes. Route 894, which the Applicants have identified as the route that best meets the

 6         Commission' s routing criteria.

 7   Q:    HOW DO YOU RESPOND TO MS. REINECKE'S FINDINGS SUMMARIZED ON

 8         PAGE 89-91 OF HER DIRECT TESTIMONY?

 9   A:    Ms. Reinecke's summarized findings states "Route CCG avoids USFWS Karst Zone 1."

10         While this statement is true, it does not mention that Route 894 also avoids USFWS Karst

11         Zone 1. Therefore, this is neither justification nor support for choosing Route CCG.


12         Ms. Reinecke's summarized findings states "Route CCG avoids the Edwards Aquifer."

13         While this statement is true, it does not mention that Route 894 also avoids the Edwards

14         Aquifer (See Exhibit CMM-3). This statement, and her testimony, fails to recognize that

15         both routes, and all links proposed by the Applicants in the EA, also cross other major

16         aquifers including the Trinity Aquifer and the Edward-Trinity Aquifer and several minor

17         aquifers including the Hickory Aquifer, Marble Falls Aquifer, and the Ellenburger-San

18         Saba Aquifer. Therefore, this is neither justification nor support for choosing Route CCG.

19         Ms. Reinecke's summarized findings states "Route CCG avoids the ESSS portion of the

20         Colorado River." As shown in Ms. Reinecke's Exhibit RLSR-0.4, neither Route 894 nor

21         Route CCG crosses the ESSS portion of the Colorado River. And neither does Link J24,

22         which is not a link utilized in either route. Therefore, this is neitherjustification nor support

23         for choosing Route CCG.

     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                     5            Cross-Rebuttal Testimony & Exhibits
     PUC Docket No. 59475                                                of Christine M. Magers, CWB
  1         Ms. Reinecke' s summarized findings states "Route CCG avoids crossing the Rocky Creek

 2         ESSS, which is crossed by Route 894." But it moves the route closer to Clear Creek and

 3         San Saba River ESSS at N4 and 03. Which, if reviewed at the watershed level is a larger

 4         cumulative impact versus only looking at the direct stream crossing location impact.

 5         Ms. Reinecke's summarized findings states "Route CCG results in only one ES S S crossing.

 6         This crossing is located in a highly constrained portion of the Study Area." Route 894 has

 7         only two ESSS crossings. Therefore, this is neither justification nor support for choosing

 8         Route CCG.

 9         Ms. Reinecke' s summarized findings states "Route CCG avoids all other CWA Section

10         303(d) impaired waters." Both Route CCG and Route 894 only cross San Saba River once.

11         Therefore, this is neither justification nor support for choosing Route CCG.

12         Ms. Reinecke' s summarized findings states "Route CCG avoids critical habitat for the

13         Texas fatmucket associated with Cherokee Creek, which is crossed twice by Route 894."

14         While it is true that Route 894 crosses critical habitat in Cherokee Creek, it leaves out the

15         fact that Route CCG also crosses Cherokee Creek just upstream of the critical habitat.

16         Without this detail, this statement is misleading.


17         Several bullet items in Ms. Reinecke' s summarized findings discuss habitat fragmentation-

18         sensitive areas without considering property boundaries. PUCT Routing Criteria reviews

19         routes that parallel property boundaries, not parcel boundaries. Her analysis would be

20         applicable to route analysis if it considered the PUCT routing criteria for paralleling

21         property boundaries along with the EMST aggregate landcover dataset to review

22         fragmentation-sensitive habitat. Because her analysis did not include property boundaries,

23         it fails to recognize the importance of maintaining the continuity of properties that are

     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                    6           Cross-Rebuttal Testimony & Exhibits
     PUC Docket No. 59475                                              of Christine M. Magers, CWB
  1         owned and managed by a single entity or person that also contains fragmentation-sensitive

 2         habitat. As an example, Link N4 on Route CCG should not be used as it cuts a large

 3         property, made of several parcels, in half that provides Golden Cheeked Warbler habitat as

 4         well as other native wildlife and protected species habitat.

 5                               II.          RECOMMENDATION

 6   Q:    BASED ON THE INTERVENOR TESTIMONY YOU REVIEWED, HAVE YOU

 7         CHANGED THE RECOMMENDATIONS IN YOUR DIRECT TESTIMONY?

 8   A:    Only slightly, and that is in regard to Link N4 discussed above; the Commission should not

 9         site a transmission line on the new route CCG proposed by Ms. Reinecke.


10                                     III.     CONCLUSION


11   Q:    DOES THIS CONCLUDE YOUR DIRECT TESTIMONY?

12   A:    Yes; however, I reserve the right to supplement or amend my cross-rebuttal testimony and

13         to present additional cross-rebuttal testimony if necessary.
